To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PG inhibits the growth of Cal u-6 lung cells and induces apoptosis, which is accompanied by the loss mitochondrial membrane potential (DeltaPsi(m)).
MEK inhibitor slightly prevents growth inhibition and death by PG in Calu- 6 cells.
PG inhibits the growth of Calau-6 lung cancer cell, induces apoptosis and increases O(2)(-), which is partially prevented by MEK inhibitor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of PG in relation to MAPK inhibitors on lung cancer cells.
the effects of MAPK inhibitor on cell death in relation to ROS and GSH changes in PG-treated Calul-6 lung cancer.
the effects of polyphenols on cancer cells in relation of ROS and GSH.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the growth inhibition and death induced by PG in Calu- 6 cells were partially associated with O(2)(-)-mediated GSH depletion.
the growth inhibition and death of Calu- 6 cells by PG was partially related to ROS and GSH changes.
PG and/or MAP inhibitors can affect growth, cell death and ROS and GSH changes in Calu-3 cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PG and MAPK inhibitors can be used as potential chemopreventive agents for lung cancer.
PG and MAPK inhibitors could be used for the prevention and treatment of lung cancer in relation to O(2) (-) level and GSH contents.
the MAPK signaling pathways may be related to PG-mediated lung cancer cell death and growth inhibition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MAPK inhibitors can be used as a therapeutic agent for cancer treatment.
PG inhibited growth and induced death in Calu6 cells.
MAPK inhibitors may be used in combination with PG in cancer treatment to increase efficacy and reduce toxicity.
